clue.text: Source of cash in company's first bid

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word company's

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A firm's opening bid is where the money comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox, so figuratively a funding pot that money is drawn from.

clue.text: Block rise of company with hint about Director

indicators.note: in a down light a rise reads upwards, so the word for company is written bottom to top
about means surrounding, so the word for hint goes round the director's letter

parts.note: a hint is a clue

explanation.surface: A firm's share price climbs while a director drops a hint, and someone tries to stop it.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to obstruct or shut off, a formal synonym of the verb block.

clue.text: Force — considering everything — to be curtailed as a last resort

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: in all means taking everything into account

explanation.surface: Using force, all things weighed, should be kept short and only tried when nothing else works.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the ultimate recourse is the one that comes last, hence final; 'as a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ultimate, the closing option after all others, is final, the last in line.

clue.text: Ignore half of answer, showing error in deduction

indicators.note: letters in error are in the wrong places, so the pool is rearranged
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Skipping part of the answer gives the game away as a flawed inference.
explanation.walkthrough: IGNORE plus ANS (half of 'answer') is rearranged; 'Ignore' looks like an instruction but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the process of drawing conclusions by logic, which is what deduction means.

clue.text: Arrangement of Sondheim being purely for pleasure

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks the material, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A Sondheim score arranged simply to be enjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure as the chief good, a life lived purely for enjoyment.

clue.text: Detestable expression of surprise applied to flute playing

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of the instrument's name are played about with

explanation.surface: Someone gasps in disgust at awful flute playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hateful and detestable are synonyms, both meaning deserving loathing.

clue.text: Put off fellow stabbing game animals

indicators.note: a fellow stabbing the animals is pushed into them, so his letter goes inside

parts.note: deer are hunted as game
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A man is deterred from knifing hunted deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone, the same as putting something off.

clue.text: Negligible reason not to honour cheque?

definitions.meaning: a bank refuses a cheque drawn on an account that does not exist

explanation.surface: An unimportant excuse for a bank bouncing a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means worthless or insignificant, and literally describes the lack of a bank account.

clue.text: Former African politician having difficulty supporting position

indicators.note: in a down light the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: to sit is to take up a position
to be in a hole is to be in difficulty

explanation.surface: A one-time African leader whose career is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ndabaningi Sithole was a Zimbabwean nationalist leader who founded ZANU.
explanation.definitionFit: Sithole is a specific example: a Rhodesian and Zimbabwean nationalist leader of the 1960s to 1990s.

clue.text: Influential figure I note controlling senior officer

indicators.note: controlling means holding in check, so the first pair of letters holds the officer inside

parts.note: N is short for note, as in a banknote
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a junior is ordering a senior officer about.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered person seen as a symbol, an influential or idolised figure.

clue.text: Religious observance: 20 accepted it in a church

indicators.note: in places the group of pieces inside the letters for a church

parts.note: refers to the answer at 20 across, a word for a nobleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posh worshipper in church takes part in a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of faith is a deed showing religious belief, such as a profession or rite of observance.

clue.text: Expert not entirely accepting representation of folly in how game starts

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the trimmed word for expert holds the rearranged letters
not entirely means one letter short, here the final one

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert

indicators.note: a representation reshapes its subject, so the letters of folly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist half-accepts a silly display at the start of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: BUF holds LLYOF, the anagram of 'folly'. A bully-off is how a hockey match starts: two players tap sticks over the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In field hockey the bully-off is the face-off that starts or restarts play.

clue.text: Believe Welsh town will accommodate king after ditching baron

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the trimmed town holds the king's letter
ditching means throwing out, so the baron's letter is dropped

parts.note: Brecon is a market town in Powys, mid Wales
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A Welsh town will host a royal visit once the aristocrat has been sent packing.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to think or suppose, so it is a synonym of believe.

clue.text: Car — recalled the best sort after one disembarks

indicators.note: a passenger who disembarks gets off, so the letter for one leaves
recalled is read as called back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: the cream is the elite, the best of a group
A, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A passenger steps out of a top-of-the-range car that has been recalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is informal shorthand for a Mercedes, a make of car.

clue.text: Conservative city-dweller receiving Government refusal as "from the Stone Age"

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the citizen's word holds the next letters

parts.note: a Roman is someone from the city of Rome
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A Tory urbanite rebuffed by the government is dismissed as prehistoric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon describes early modern humans of the Upper Palaeolithic, i.e. of the Stone Age.

clue.text: Red tuna apparently like a crab

parts.note: the clue words are what you get from the reading: NATURED with ill (badly) beside it is an anagram, made badly, of the words red tuna

explanation.surface: A red tuna is apparently crustacean in appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'ill' as an anagram signal applied to NATURED, and it gives RED TUNA. 'Apparently' flags the trick; 'crab' means a grumpy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby people are grumpy and bad-tempered; the idiom 'crab' for a grouch fits ill temper.

clue.text: Mistakenly heading off that soldier I ignored in military town

indicators.note: done mistakenly means set out wrongly, so the remaining letters are rearranged
heading off means losing the head, the first letter of that
ignored means left out, so the letter I is removed from soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is waved away while wrongly heading off to a garrison town.
explanation.walkthrough: HAT and SOLDER are mixed together. Aldershot in Hampshire is the traditional home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is an example: a Hampshire town known as the home of the British Army.

clue.text: Strain hard to encircle outside of tower (historic fortress)

indicators.note: to encircle is to surround, so the strain's word goes around the tower's ends

parts.note: a strain is a tune or song

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
historic things are old

explanation.surface: Effort is needed to surround the outer wall of a tower in an ancient castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place, a direct synonym of fortress.

clue.text: Worker associated with whisky (drink much loved in France)

parts.note: tea is a drink
cher is French for dear, much loved

explanation.surface: A labourer linked with Scotch and a French drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Teacher's is a brand of blended Scotch whisky, so the worker is a schoolteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher is a working professional, and Teacher's is a well-known Scotch brand bearing that name.

clue.text: Superficial American author not popular in our day

parts.note: out means out of fashion, not currently in vogue
Artemus Ward was a 19th-century American humorist

explanation.surface: A shallow American writer is unfashionable nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward means on the surface or external, so it is a synonym of superficial.

clue.text: Noble part of family (but only part)

indicators.note: the bracket warns that only some letters across these words are wanted

explanation.surface: An aristocrat belongs to the family, but only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person, someone of noble or posh stock.

clue.text: Landholder's female rival put up charge

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is a landholder

indicators.note: in a down light, put up means written upwards

parts.note: a foe is an opponent or rival
a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A landlord's female competitor raised the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal law a feoffee is the person granted a fief, i.e. one who holds land.

clue.text: Contemporary of 8 to sanction talk at table

parts.note: a sanction can be a penalty or ban
ana is a collection of sayings, as in 'table talk'

explanation.surface: A colleague of the politician moves to outlaw dinner-table chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Canaan Banana was Zimbabwe's first president, alongside Sithole in the struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaan Banana was Zimbabwe's first president and so a peer of Sithole in that era.

clue.text: Article set to deliver financial sponsor

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: A newspaper item is prepared to bring in a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private investor who backs a venture, especially a theatre production.

clue.text: Plant in river in the past blocking lake

indicators.note: the pieces block the lake by sitting in its middle

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Vegetation in a river once dammed a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an example: an aromatic herb plant used in French cooking.

clue.text: Remote facilities — in a field, initially

indicators.note: in places the word for facilities between the two initial letters
initially takes the first letters of the two words

parts.note: facilities is a euphemism for a toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: Toilets are out in a field, far away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and standoffish, so remote in manner.

clue.text: One showcased recordings of gas circulating in pubs

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the pair of pub abbreviations

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house, doubled for pubs
O looks like the figure one

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the gas is turned back to front

parts.note: argon is a noble gas

explanation.surface: A record of gas moving round in bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'what showcased recordings': a gramophone played records before later formats.
explanation.definitionFit: The old record-player presented recorded sound to listeners, a device that showcased recordings.

clue.text: Meat product more than enough for this old ruler

indicators.note: the meat word has one letter too many for the ruler, so the surplus is cut

parts.note: offal is meat from organs such as liver and kidneys

explanation.surface: A plate of offal is too much for an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was the Anglo-Saxon king of Mercia, an example of an old ruler.

clue.text: It's a ship, guaranteed

definitions.meaning: a 19th-century warship clad with iron plates
a cast-iron, watertight assurance cannot fail

explanation.surface: A boat with a warranty.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is an armoured warship; the adjective means rigid and certain, unbreakable.

clue.text: Half-heartedly fund, returning charge? That's sweet

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is reversed
half-heartedly means losing half of the heart, one of the two central letters

parts.note: to foot a bill is to fund it
a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Grudgingly paying a refunded charge is a nice result.
explanation.walkthrough: FOOT loses one middle O to give FOT, which turns back to TOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection, so an example of a sweet.
